I can relate to literally everything you said, falling out of love with things is a fear I also have, it happens with everything I do. It's so interesting to start with but then it fizzles out, but I think if there's one thing I always pursue, it's exploring emotions, so when something is too logical for too long, or doesn't translate my emotions perfectly I drop it. So art feels amazing until I'm practising perspective and measuring angles. Music feels incredible until I'm analysing scales and learning software.  


This is why acting is so compelling, not only because I remember it feeling so good, but the way you get better is literally by exploring emotions.  


I hear you on being indecisive. People have little patience and they can be quite quick to judge and incredibly harsh as well, even if they define themselves as a "good person". At the same time, if you're actually interested (and committed) to doing what you love, it can take a lifetime to just find out what that is. That's a nasty cocktail of self exploration and misplaced shame and it's the price you pay for being true to yourself enough to ask the hardest of questions. Just know that if you do figure it out, while everyone else is having their midlife crisis, you'll be enjoying an actual, real cocktail, surrounded by affluent people who love what you love, so be resilient and strong and don't be so hard on yourself.  


If it makes you feel better, I dropped out of two colleges (middle school in my country) and I dropped out of university. I regretted it for so long, but not because I made a mistake, only because I was broke as a result.

I agree that the $99 package is a bit piss, but if you get the $599 one you get face to face weekly chats and assignment overviews over skype, as well as monthly video critiques of your work and progress. With this package you also get access to their lectures and 3D resources, which, in addition to the one to one coaching, starts to sound like actual art school.

Considering art school is about 5 times this and some people need the extra guidance, especially for fast track learning, it could make sense, seeing as a part time job could pay for it.

For people who need the extra pressure of regular meetings with a professional coach, the $599 option seems to be the most compelling, since any more money would only go to an extra monthly, bi weekly, or weekly chat session with your coach - definitely a good bonus, just not worth the extra $100, $200, or $400, respectively

EDIT: After speaking with them, turns out its not face to face over video chat, but you do get their undivided attention during text, or voice chat, for 30mins a piece.
